questions.q: What can CROSS APPLY / LATERAL do that a plain JOIN cannot?
options: Let the right-hand derived table reference columns from a table earlier in the same FROM clause
Join more than two tables at once
Filter rows with a WHERE clause
Return aggregated results without GROUP BY
questions.explain: A plain JOIN's right-hand side is evaluated independently; CROSS APPLY/LATERAL lets a derived table be correlated to — i.e. reference columns from — a preceding table, row by row.

questions.q: In T-SQL, what's the difference between CROSS APPLY and OUTER APPLY?
options: CROSS APPLY drops rows with no match (like an inner join); OUTER APPLY keeps them with NULLs (like a left join)
CROSS APPLY is faster but returns the same rows as OUTER APPLY
OUTER APPLY only works with table-valued functions, CROSS APPLY only works with subqueries
There is no real difference between them
questions.explain: This mirrors the familiar inner-join/left-join distinction, just applied to a correlated derived table instead of a plain table.

questions.q: Which keyword does PostgreSQL use for the same concept as T-SQL's CROSS APPLY?
options: LATERAL, combined with JOIN (e.g. CROSS JOIN LATERAL)
APPLY, used exactly like T-SQL
CORRELATE
PostgreSQL has no equivalent at all
questions.explain: PostgreSQL has supported LATERAL for exactly this purpose for years; the concept is identical to CROSS APPLY, only the keyword differs.

questions.q: Since which MySQL version does MySQL support LATERAL?
options: MySQL 8.0.14
MySQL 5.7
MySQL 8.0.0 (LATERAL has always existed in MySQL 8)
MySQL does not support LATERAL at all
questions.explain: MySQL added LATERAL support specifically in version 8.0.14, later than the initial MySQL 8.0 release.

questions.q: Which dialect supports BOTH the LATERAL keyword and its own CROSS APPLY/OUTER APPLY syntax?
options: Oracle (12c+), which added CROSS APPLY/OUTER APPLY specifically to ease migration from SQL Server
T-SQL, which supports LATERAL alongside APPLY
MySQL, which supports CROSS APPLY alongside LATERAL
PostgreSQL, which supports CROSS APPLY alongside LATERAL
questions.explain: Oracle added LATERAL support in 12c and later added its own CROSS APPLY/OUTER APPLY syntax, specifically to make migrating T-SQL code to Oracle easier.
